description:
# NodeRouter missed-line coverage plan

Status: planning only; no tests or production changes implemented or executed.
Target: `lib/zaq/node_router.ex`; supplied baseline 93%, missed lines 107, 112,
114, 117, 209, 252, 253, 360. These line locations were verified against live source.
The percentage was supplied by the coordinator, not independently remeasured.

## Scope and evidence

Read `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agent-tools.md`, `docs/testing-approach.md`, the NodeRouter
dispatch contract in `docs/architecture.md`, and the relevant Engine overview,
startup, data flow and design decisions in `docs/services/engine.md`. Also consulted
workflow, setup and documentation policies. Loaded `test-coverage-planner`.
Serena successfully returned live source/test overviews and definitions; no semantic
fallback was necessary. Bounded text queries verified exact missed-line mappings,
related test ownership, test configuration and Mix aliases.

Inspected the real `Zaq.NodeRouter`, `Zaq.Event`, BO API delegation and
`InternalBoundaries.default_handle_event/2`, plus both existing router test files
and router stubs. Existing tests already cover successful fanout, explicit discovery
errors, zero targets, ordinary dispatch RPC failures, action fallback, consumed hops,
async diagnostics and confidentiality. The additions below complement those tests.

Action reuse assessment: **N/A — tests only**. No executable production operation,
Action, domain API, tool exposure or dependency seam is being designed or changed.
The legacy invoke compatibility wrapper is itself an explicit coverage target;
testing it does not recommend new production invoke consumers.

`bw prime` and read-only inspection of existing issue `zaq-n82` found historical
whole-file coverage follow-up, not proof of current coverage. No issue changes are
part of this plan. User authorization to preserve the dirty tree resolves the prime
warning about existing changes. The observed pre-existing changes are:

- `test/e2e/specs/system_config.spec.js`
- `test/e2e/support/bo.js`
- `test/e2e/support/people-auth-browser.cjs`
- `test/zaq_web/people_browser_test.exs`

## Exact ownership and implementation order

1. **New `test/zaq/node_router_contract_test.exs`, module
   `Zaq.NodeRouterContractTest`, `use ExUnit.Case, async: true`,
   `use ExUnitProperties`.** Owns injected-runtime fanout scenarios A–E and the
   malformed-hop property. These scenarios have no global mutations and use
   confidential envelopes to avoid unrelated workflow observers.
2. **Existing `test/zaq/node_router_test.exs`, module `Zaq.NodeRouterTest`, retain
   `async: false`.** Add a `describe "default RPC transport"` for F and a
   `describe "invoke/5 compatibility"` for G. This module already owns real
   registered-process routing and legacy invoke examples. No module-wide setup,
   existing assertion changes, or conversion of other tests is required.
3. Coordinator runs the focused validation below and reports each requested line,
   rather than declaring success from a percentage alone.

No other source, test/support, test configuration, Git or Beadwork modifications
are required. `test/zaq/confidential_event_test.exs` is a focused regression
companion, unchanged. No DB fixtures, DataCase, external network, browser or E2E
coverage is needed for these routing contracts.

## Shared setup and callback rules

Use real `Event.new/3`, `EventHop` structs and public NodeRouter entry points.
Construct explicit events with deterministic timestamps such as
`~U[2026-01-01 00:00:00Z]`, a per-test trace marker, and meaningful actor/assigns
markers when testing preservation. Save `original_hop = event.next_hop` before
dispatch. Acknowledgment expectations can use the independently stated envelope
change: original request/actor/assigns/opts/trace retained, `next_hop: nil`,
`hops: [original_hop]`, and the scenario's exact response.

For A–E, use BO role/action `:unsupported_node_router_coverage_action`, request
`%{probe: :fanout}`, and `opts: [action: :unsupported_node_router_coverage_action,
confidential: true]`. A synthetic unsupported action is only for router error/
transport testing; it is not a proposed domain action. E returns controlled
acknowledgments at the RPC boundary and never calls a real role API.

Default controlled runtime values:

- `current_node_fn: fn -> :local@host end`
- `node_list_fn: fn -> [] end`
- `whereis_fn: fn _supervisor -> nil end`

Specify overrides visibly in each scenario. Capture `owner = self()` and
`marker = make_ref()` in the test process. Discovery/execution callbacks send
`{marker, ...}` messages to `owner`. Return `owner` as a deterministic PID for a
found supervisor; never spawn a disposable process merely to obtain a PID.

**Do not put assertions or `flunk` inside callbacks used by `dispatch_all/2`.**
Its rescue/catch can swallow an ExUnit assertion and, in failure tests, accidentally
produce the exact expected error. Record arguments/calls and assert afterward.
Likewise do not assert anything inside a deliberately raised/thrown function.
Use narrow patterns plus a catch-all that records `{:unexpected_call, args}` when
negative-call detection matters. After the synchronous public call has returned,
`assert_received`/`refute_received` provides a completion-safe check without sleeps.

Use no Mox in these additions: NodeRouter is the implementation under test and
already exposes runtime functions for node/RPC boundaries. Inspected
`NodeRouterStubs.stub_passthrough/0` changes global Mox mode and blanket-stubs the
router; `NodeRouterPassthroughStub` bypasses routing altogether. Neither is suitable.
Keep runtime maps inline initially; extract a private test helper only if genuine
duplication remains. No new production hooks, public helpers or test flags.

## A — line 107: reject asynchronous fanout before discovery

Suggested test name: `"rejects async fanout without discovery or task startup"`.

- Build the common event with `type: :async` and an empty hops list.
- Override all runtime callbacks (current node, peer list, local lookup, RPC and
  async startup) to record unexpected use. Return safe values if called so a
  mistaken implementation cannot create a task or network operation.
- Call `NodeRouter.dispatch_all(event, runtime)`.
- Assert exact `{:error, {:invalid_fanout, :async_hop}}`.
- Assert no marker-tagged callback messages: in particular no discovery, execution
  or task scheduling. This establishes rejection before fanout work, not merely
  an error after attempted execution.
- Do not assert a returned consumed Event: the API returns an error tuple here.
- Covers line 107. Confidentiality only suppresses the incidental observer path;
  it does not change hop consumption or async rejection.

## B — line 112: normalize a discovery exception

Suggested test name: `"normalizes raised discovery failures to the requested role"`.

- Common sync BO event. Local lookup returns nil; peer list is
  `[:broken@host]`.
- `rpc_call_with_timeout_fn` records the full invocation, then raises
  `RuntimeError, "controlled discovery failure"` for
  `(:broken@host, Process, :whereis, [ZaqWeb.Endpoint], 30_000)`.
- Any execution or unmatched callback records an unexpected-call message.
- Call `dispatch_all/2` and assert exact
  `{:error, {:node_discovery_failed, :bo}}` — requested **role**, unlike ordinary
  returned badrpc discovery failures, which identify a peer.
- After return, assert the exact discovery message including timeout and refute
  execution/unexpected-call messages. This proves the exception occurred during
  discovery, not from an assertion or incidental error elsewhere.
- Covers line 112. Do not raise from the handler after dispatch starts: that would
  mix discovery failure normalization with partial fanout execution semantics.

## C — line 114: normalize throws and catchable exits during discovery

Suggested tests: `"normalizes discovery throws"` and
`"normalizes catchable discovery exits"`.

- Same input and runtime shape as B, except the discovery callback records its
  invocation then uses `throw(:controlled_discovery_throw)` or
  `exit(:controlled_discovery_exit)` respectively.
- Assert exact `{:error, {:node_discovery_failed, :bo}}` for each public call.
- Assert the precise discovery call and no execution/unexpected call afterward.
- Both exercise line 114 and distinguish the two catch classes. Small explicit
  cases are preferable to a broad generator for these finite failure mechanisms.
- `exit/1` raises a catchable exit in the calling process. Do not send exit signals,
  enable `trap_exit`, kill a process, or modify supervision to manufacture it.

## D — line 117: missing or malformed next hop rejects before routing

Example test: `"rejects a missing fanout next hop"`.

- Construct `%Event{request: %{probe: :fanout}, next_hop: nil}`.
- Pass a runtime whose callbacks record any use.
- Assert exact `{:error, {:invalid_event, :missing_or_invalid_next_hop}}`.
- Assert no runtime callback messages. No PubSub subscription is needed.

Property: `"non-struct hop maps never become routable fanout destinations"`.

- Invariant: a plain map is not an EventHop, even if its destination/type look
  valid; malformed routing metadata must not initiate discovery/execution.
- Generate a bounded map with at most 3 entries, keys drawn from
  `[:destination, :type, :timestamp]` and values from a bounded combination of
  fixed atoms (`:bo`, `:sync`, `:async`), integers and short binaries. Include an
  explicit concrete `%{destination: :bo, type: :sync}` example so the plausible
  malformed shape is guaranteed, independent of generator choices. Never generate
  `:__struct__` and thereby accidentally manufacture an EventHop.
- Use `max_runs: 20`, `max_length: 24` for binaries and bounded integers. For each
  generated map set `event.next_hop` to it, allocate a fresh marker and invoke the
  same public API. Assert the exact invalid-event tuple and zero callback messages.
- Optional tiny example table `[false, :bad_hop, [], "bo", 42]` checks non-map
  representatives without a Cartesian product. These are valid inputs for the
  explicit defensive fallback, not invented downstream handler states.
- Covers line 117 (and its return expression). No missing-key struct construction:
  `%Event{}` requires both request and next_hop at compile time.
- Do not expand this property to arbitrary non-map runtime arguments or unsupported
  hop types: those are separate input-contract questions, not this coverage gap.

## E — line 209: skip a peer that has no role supervisor and continue discovery

Suggested test name: `"skips empty peers and still fans out to later owners"`.

- Common sync BO event, no local supervisor. Peers in declared order:
  `[:empty@host, :owner@host]`.
- Timeout-aware RPC callback returns nil for empty peer discovery and captured
  `owner` PID for owner-peer discovery; records both requests.
- For owner-peer execution, record
  `(:owner@host, Zaq.Bo.Api, :handle_event, [routed, action, nil], :infinity)`
  and return `%{routed | response: {:ack, :owner@host}}`.
- Assert exact `{:ok, [acknowledgment]}` with response
  `{:ack, :owner@host}`, unchanged request/actor/assigns/opts/trace, exactly the
  original hop in history and nil next_hop.
- Assert both discovery requests with `30_000`, the single execution request
  with `:infinity`, and the consumed envelope passed to that request.
- Refute execution on `:empty@host` and any unmatched call. Do not assert incidental
  message ordering; the public result and observed set of calls prove continuation.
- Covers line 209 with nonempty continuation, which the existing zero-target test
  (empty peer list) does not exercise.

## F — lines 252–253: exercise real default RPC locally

Owner: existing serialized `Zaq.NodeRouterTest`, new default-transport describe.
Suggested test name: `"uses default RPC for discovery and role execution on this VM"`.

- Capture `actual_node = node()`; assert `Process.whereis(ZaqWeb.Endpoint)` is a
  PID as an explicit existing-application prerequisite. Do not start/replace the
  endpoint. This prerequisite is already used by current router tests.
- Pick synthetic current node from two fixed atoms so it is guaranteed different
  from `actual_node` (choose `:router_probe_a@host`, unless equal, then
  `:router_probe_b@host`). Do not create runtime atoms dynamically.
- Runtime: `current_node_fn` returns that synthetic value, `node_list_fn` returns
  `[actual_node]`, and `whereis_fn` returns nil. **Omit both RPC callback keys.**
- Construct a confidential sync BO event with the intentionally unsupported
  action `:unsupported_node_router_coverage_action` and visible request/actor/
  assigns markers. Call real `NodeRouter.dispatch(event, runtime)`.
- Because router-current differs from the actual node, discovery takes the remote
  path. Its default `:rpc.call(actual_node, Process, :whereis, [ZaqWeb.Endpoint],
  30_000)` executes on this VM. Execution likewise uses real default RPC to the
  local BO API with timeout `:infinity`.
- Assert the exact resulting envelope, with response
  `{:error, {:unsupported_action, :unsupported_node_router_coverage_action}}`,
  consumed original hop, nil next_hop, and all request/context fields preserved.
  This response is owned by real `InternalBoundaries.default_handle_event/2`;
  no invented successful domain action or business/DB fixture is involved.
- Covers lines 252 and 253 in both discovery and execution. It tests ZAQ's default
  transport wiring, not merely an isolated call to Erlang RPC.
- This is a local-RPC integration test, **not proof of distributed peer behavior**.
  No `Node.start`, `Node.connect`, epmd, cookies, peers, external host, or network
  fault is necessary. Local `:rpc.call(node(), ...)` works without distributed mode.
- Synchronous return is the completion barrier. No task mock, monitor or sleep
  is needed. If the endpoint prerequisite is absent, report environment failure;
  do not silently skip or start global processes just for coverage.

## G — line 360: legacy invoke preserves the complete RPC failure tuple

Owner: existing `Zaq.NodeRouterTest`, new invoke/5 compatibility describe.
Suggested test name: `"invoke preserves remote RPC failure details"`.

- Call `NodeRouter.invoke(:bo, String, :upcase, ["hello"], runtime)` directly.
  This specific test must use invoke: dispatch alone cannot reach unwrapping.
- Runtime current `:local@host`, peers `[:remote@host]`, local lookup nil.
- Timeout-aware RPC discovery for `ZaqWeb.Endpoint` returns captured owner PID.
  Execution to `Zaq.Bo.Api.handle_event/3` records the envelope/action/context and
  returns `{:badrpc, :timeout}`.
- Assert exact public value `{:error, {:rpc_failed, :remote@host, :timeout}}`.
  Assert it is the returned tuple, not an Event, nested error, or bare reason.
- Assert recorded RPC action `:invoke`, context nil, request exactly
  `%{module: String, function: :upcase, args: ["hello"]}`, nil next_hop, one BO
  sync hop, discovery timeout `30_000` and execution timeout `:infinity`.
  The wrapper generates timestamp/trace, so assert valid binary trace and hop
  destination/type, without assuming a predetermined UUID or wall-clock time.
- No real RPC occurs; no mock of NodeRouter or private unwrap function is allowed.
- The wrapper broadcasts a public unnamed event. This is existing compatibility
  behavior (already tested in `confidential_event_test.exs`); use only harmless
  request data and do not attach a global observer for this scenario.
- Covers line 360. Its body and the following general unwrap clause currently
  return the same value. The public contract cannot distinguish deleting this
  redundant specialization; do not fabricate a behavioral distinction or assert
  private clause execution. Coverage is the evidence for the requested line.

## Isolation, reachability and exceptions

- All eight requested lines are reachable through public APIs with existing seams.
  No unreachable-line exemption or coverage suppression is currently justified.
- New A–E tests remain async-safe: callback state is process-local, there are no
  named processes or shared mutable resources, and confidential events avoid
  observer side effects. They call real routing code and do not mutate application
  configuration, registry entries, ETS, persistent terms, logger or Mox mode.
- F belongs with existing serialized real-runtime tests because it relies on the
  running fixed-name endpoint and runtime RPC service. It only reads their state;
  `async: false` does not authorize interfering with them. G stays with its
  existing compatibility owner; it introduces no global mutation.
- No new global resource therefore requires snapshot/restore. If implementation
  discovers a genuinely unavoidable global change, stop and revise the plan:
  isolate it in a dedicated `async: false` owner, preserve absent-versus-present
  configuration, register `on_exit` restoration before mutation, and demonstrate
  why the existing runtime map cannot express the behavior. Do not quietly add it.
- Do not kill/restart PubSub, role supervisors, task supervisors, or endpoint to
  force rescue/catch/RPC branches. Do not use node disconnects, timeout waits,
  uncaught `:kill`, VM distribution changes, hot-patching, `:meck`, or private
  function exposure. These are unsafe or unnecessary approaches, not coverage
  requirements.
- No elapsed-time assertions, sleeps, polling, or unmanaged child processes.
  Do not add telemetry handlers: these lines do not concern async diagnostics.
- Property testing is justified for malformed hop-map rejection over a broad
  value space. The remaining discrete transport/error examples are clearer as
  examples. Existing confidentiality properties provide the security companion.
- Whole-file coverage need not equal the supplied baseline under a different
  focused test selection. Report run scope, denominator and remaining lines; do
  not promise 100% or suppress other pre-existing gaps.

## Focused coordinator commands and acceptance

Run from repository root with the coordinator's existing test environment and
isolated test database. The Mix test alias performs database creation/migrations
even though these particular tests need no records. Do not change database config
or run against a developer data store to bypass setup failures.

1. After implementation, coordinator runs `mix q` through Context Mode.
2. Run only the owning tests and unchanged confidentiality companion:

   `mix test test/zaq/node_router_contract_test.exs test/zaq/node_router_test.exs test/zaq/confidential_event_test.exs`

3. When collecting the requested line evidence, use the same bounded selection:

   `MIX_ENV=test mix coveralls.json test/zaq/node_router_contract_test.exs test/zaq/node_router_test.exs test/zaq/confidential_event_test.exs`

   The coverage invocation also executes those tests; it can replace step 2 when
   the coordinator wants one targeted execution with coverage. Parse only
   `source_files[]` where `name == "lib/zaq/node_router.ex"` in
   `cover/excoveralls.json`, report covered/relevant lines and the counts at
   zero-based indexes 106, 111, 113, 116, 208, 251, 252 and 359. Each requested
   executable line must have a positive count. Remap if source changes first.

For debugging, restrict to the failing file/test line after implementation. Do not
rerun broader tests without a new failure, change or unresolved concern. No full
suite, stale-test sweep, precommit or E2E run is proposed by this task.

`mix q` is not read-only: the inspected alias includes `format` and
`deps.unlock --unused`. The coordinator must preserve the existing dirty changes
and review any resulting modifications, never reset/stash/overwrite unrelated
work. Do not run q during this planning-only pass.

Acceptance: A–G and the property have exact public assertions; no callback
assertion can be swallowed by fanout rescue; all requested line counts are
positive or a specific newly verified limitation is reported; targeted tests and
q results are recorded with their actual scope. No test or validation success is
claimed by this planning artifact.


Coordinator execution override: tests only in assigned files, preserve pre-existing edits; no worker Mix/Git/Beadwork mutations. Coordinator alone runs mix q and added/edited tests --cover. No full-suite or precommit execution for this coverage task.
